verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's docs say the browser extension autofills saved passkeys, and that the integrated authenticator automatically generates TOTP codes. The extension also enters matching credentials into login fields. However, no evidence explicitly says the extension fills the TOTP code into the login's 2FA step rather than just generating it. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of TOTP autofill or copy during browser login, and independent hands-on corroboration of passkey and TOTP autofill in the extension.

support.subject: As an everyday user, a browser extension autofills my TOTP codes and passkeys during login instead of making me retype them

citations.quote: Save passkeys in your Bitwarden vault and use the browser extension or mobile apps to autofill them across the apps and websites you use every day.
it automatically produces the time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs), six-digit codes using SHA-1 that rotate every 30 seconds
When you visit a website, the browser extension recognizes it and enters matching credentials from your vault into the login fields.
